--- description: "Design spec, seat directory, tokens, the official icon set and a reusable-source knowledge base for DeepSeek Harness plugin authors." --- # DeepSeek Design Resources

Making community plugins look like one product.
Spec · Seat directory · Design tokens · Official icon set · Reusable source · Live component gallery

简体中文 · English

--- ## Why this exists DeepSeek Harness publicly provides **Cordis plugin APIs, slots, semantic tokens, UI primitives and client development guidance**. The relevant rules are distributed across GitHub documentation, agent guidance and source code; they are not yet organized as a complete design handbook around community plugin authors' interface tasks. So plugins each do their own thing, and one screen ends up with mismatched button heights, arbitrary spacing and unpredictable stacking. That is not a plugin's fault — it is what happens without a spec and a check. This repository organizes those references into a guide community plugin authors can discover and verify. Three rules: 1. **No invented numbers.** Every size, gap and duration carries its source (the official client bundle, Apple HIG, OpenHarmony, or an explicit "this repository suggests"). Where no authority exists, it says so instead of inventing something that looks professional. 2. **No arbitrary taste verdicts.** Visual quality is assessed through checkable criteria such as hierarchy, reading width, density, alignment, theme contrast and interaction feedback. 3. **If it cannot be decided, it is not a rule.** "Spacing should feel comfortable" is not a rule. "Two adjacent independent controls closer than 16px count as cramped" is. Every document states whether its criteria can be checked automatically. ## Layout | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | [`spec/`](spec/) | 12 documents: region map, frame layout, seat selection, centre-column occupancy, controls, tokens, motion, icons, accessibility, checklist, conflict arbitration | | [`rules/`](rules/) | `rules.json` / `rules.csv` — the checklist in machine-readable form, for CI gates and auditors | | [`guides/`](guides/) | Task-oriented guides: overview, official basis, principles, interface patterns, seats and integration, verification and sources | | [`data/`](data/) | Collected from a running harness: 75 icons, 90 seats, tokens (palette 77 / light aliases 115 / dark aliases 119 / scale and type 207) and the element inventory. Calibers and capture times: [`docs/FACTS-2026-10-02.md`](docs/FACTS-2026-10-02.md) | | [`icons/`](icons/) | 75 official icons plus brand marks, exported verbatim (see [`icons/README.md`](icons/README.md)) | | [`components/`](components/) | Reusable-source knowledge base: categorised, dependency-free React built on official tokens | | [`website/`](website/) | The plugin design guide and live component gallery, with navigation, article content, on-page contents and search | | [`scripts/`](scripts/) | Collection and generation — every number here is reproducible, nothing is hand-recorded | ## Open the site Published on GitHub Pages: ``` https://physicolor.github.io/dsh-design-resources/ ``` The site is **zero-build and works straight from disk** as well: ``` website/index.html ``` Or serve it locally (no cache, so a refresh always shows current files): ```sh node scripts/serve.mjs # → http://127.0.0.1:4173/ ``` Every specimen renders as **live HTML**, not a mockup image, because these components were built with the WebUI stack in the first place. Pages on the left, the component in the middle, the rationale on the right ("why it is designed this way / when to reach for it / where the geometry comes from"). The site follows this repository's own spec, so it is the spec's first implementation rather than just a description of it: - **the spec embeds runnable demos, not screenshots**: the region map of one screen (what the left, centre and right columns are each made of after you open a new conversation; the pointer marks whichever band it sweeps over), the three-column frame (hover any column and it is picked out), the composer's vertical structure, the right rail opening and closing, the geometry of an official icon (board, safe area, bounding shape, stroke weight), the app-icon board (50 × 50 container, 36 × 36 artwork, the ink's circumscribed circle measured live), the control board (nine live readouts, five states, three counter-examples), the token board (six radii, four elevations, eight type roles, the same aliases resolved in both themes), the accessibility board (contrast computed from the WCAG formula, hit areas measured), the pre-flight checklist (clickable; one unchecked mandatory item blocks the release), the conflict board (real occupancy records; shuffle registration order and watch the order change) and the rule/source legend — all native HTML, hoverable, clickable, copyable. **Every spec document must carry an operable demo**, and the build enforces it (`every spec carries an operable demo` plus a per-page probe that crosses shadow boundaries, so a replica that silently fails to mount cannot pass as a demo) — an empty stage counts as a failure; - **the spec embeds a reproduction of the product interface, not a diagram**: the three-column frame, the composer's vertical structure and the right rail opening are the same `website/shell/` instance — every number taken from `docs/reference/` (boxes and computed styles harvested from the running product: the frame in `geometry.json`, the composer in `composer-geometry.json`, the conversation column in `conversation-geometry.json`, the top strip in `top-strip.json`, the dock under the card in `status-line.json`), and you can drag and click it directly; - **the rule for reproducing anything is screenshot first, measure second, build third**: `docs/reference/` holds photographs of the real product, and any interface has to be explainable against them — if there is no source, it does not get drawn; - **components are marked "ships with the product" or "proposed here"**: 3 of the 26 have no official counterpart at all (key-value list, mini bar, panel seat); they are this repository's proposals for plugin authors, and the page says plainly that the product has no such interface. The other 23 trace back to the product's own CSS modules or to the official primitives. A wrong label fails the build: every id in `components/origins.json` must sit in exactly one list, and every proposed component must name the real scene it serves; - **the index is a foldable tree**: groups are captions rather than toggles (a caption that hides its own contents saves height and loses the answer to "what is in here"), only component categories fold — and **the whole row is the fold control**: closed it looks exactly like its leaf siblings (text and chevron, no box), and opening it lights the same pill; the row you are actually on is bolded on top of that, so "open" and "you are here" stay two separate signals; - **specimens have no frame**: the live content sits directly on the page instead of in a box inside a box; - **each column scrolls on its own** while the page itself never does, under a liquid-glass top bar content passes behind; - **both rails drag to resize** (arrow keys work too) and remember their width and collapsed state; - **either rail collapses entirely**, with an animated open/close; - **Chinese and English, both complete**: the spec, the guides, the component documents and every specimen exist in both languages. Any Chinese left on an English page is a product string quoted verbatim, and it is followed by its English gloss. The contract and its gates are in [`docs/I18N.md`](docs/I18N.md); - **light and dark are both authored** — a design that survives light mode and collapses in dark mode counts as a defect here; - **an operable motion bench** on the motion spec page: compare the five durations and both curves side by side, which is the one thing paper cannot do and an HTML reference can; - **specimens re

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness bundle: Windows desktop operation as discrete tool calls, each returning the frames captured around the call.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-computer-control

A DeepSeek Harness bundle that turns Windows desktop operation into discrete tool
calls. Every call performs exactly one action and returns the frames captured from
just before that action until a settle period after it, so the model never has to
remember to take a screenshot.

## Installing

`dsh plugin` forwards its arguments verbatim to pnpm in the profile directory, so a
checkout, a git specifier, or a published tarball are all installed the same way:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add <path-to-this-checkout>
```

The peer dependencies (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`,
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`) are supplied by the harness, so this package declares them
rather than depending on them, and a checkout normally has no `node_modules` of its own.

DeepSeek Harness does not accept external pull requests; the documented way for a
community plugin to be found is a public repository carrying the `dsh-plugin` GitHub
topic, which is why `package.json` lists it under `keywords`.

The suites under `test/` resolve their imports against this checkout and against the
harness packages, so they run from any working directory once the peers are installed:

```sh
npm test          # or: node test/run-all.mjs
```

## What you get

Eleven tools, registered on the host `tools` service:

| Tool | One call does | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `computer_probe` | Nothing; reports screen geometry, pointer position and shape, and the window under the pointer | Text only, no image |
| `computer_screenshot` | Nothing; captures the screen, or a rectangle at an integer zoom | One image |
| `computer_move` | Moves the pointer | Frames around the move |
| `computer_click` | Presses and releases one button once | Frames around the click |
| `computer_drag` | Presses, sweeps, releases | Frames across the gesture |
| `computer_scroll` | One wheel gesture | Frames around the gesture |
| `computer_type` | Types a string as Unicode keystrokes | Frames while the text lands |
| `computer_key` | Presses and releases one named key | Frames around the key |
| `computer_chord` | Holds modifiers, presses one key, releases everything | Frames around the chord |
| `computer_wait` | Injects nothing and watches | Frames over the wait |
| `computer_frames` | Reads the recorded frames between two earlier frames | Up to the tool's own `maxFrames` (default 16); at most `maxAttachedImages` of them arrive as images and the rest are printed as paths |

`computer_frames` is the only tool that takes no new capture: it re-reads the recorder ring between two frames a previous call returned, which is how a two-frame envelope is enough to reconstruct the motion between them without paying for more images on every call.

### Reading between two returned frames

A call captures ten to thirty frames and returns two of them. `computer_frames` reaches back into the
recorder ring for the rest of that span:

```markdown
<computer-control action="frames">
result: ok
from: <the earlier frame the call printed>
to: <the later frame the call printed>
span: 1995 ms
recorded between them: 21 frame(s); returned: 4
achieved rate: 1.78 fps
attached: 2 of 4 returned frame(s), the bound that keeps one call's cost predictable
note: sampled 4 of 21 recorded frames at 2 fps; a higher fps returns more of them; stopped at the 4-frame bound; narrow the span or lower fps to see all of it
frames (offset relative to the earlier frame):
0. +0 ms | 1024x576 | 51399 bytes | image attached | <path>
1. +587 ms | 1024x576 | 51389 bytes | image attached | <path>
2. +1121 ms | 1024x576 | 51304 bytes | path only, read it with read_image | <path>
3. +1686 ms | 1024x576 | 51303 bytes | path only, read it with read_image | <path>
</computer-control>
```

Two things in that envelope are deliberate. `recorded between them` reports what the ring held, so a
thin answer is distinguishable from a span the recorder never covered, and `attached` names how many
of the listed frames arrived as images: the bound is `maxAttachedImages`, which exists to keep one
call's cost predictable, so frames past it are saved and printed as paths rather than attached. An
unattached frame can be read later with `read_image` instead of being asked for again, for as long as
the deployment's screenshot directory keeps it: that directory holds the most recent
`SHOT_RETENTION` files, after which the oldest saved paths stop resolving and a later request for one
says so rather than reporting a missing file.

## Discrete by design

There is no hold, repeat, macro, loop, or "run this until" parameter, and no way to
leave a button or a key down across calls:

- `computer_click` sends its press and release in one injected batch.
- `computer_key` and `computer_chord` release every key they press inside the same call.
- `computer_drag` is one atomic gesture; its step count is bounded by `maxDragSteps`.
- Every tool is registered as concurrency-unsafe, so the registry serializes desktop input.
- `computer_scroll` refuses a zero-notch gesture instead of reporting a no-op as success.

To click twice, call `computer_click` twice. Each call then comes back with its own frames.

## Configuration

Every value below is a `Config` field; override the row in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`, restating the keys you keep, because a patch replaces a row's
whole `config`.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `capturesPerSecond` | `10` | Frame rate the recorder produces |
| `maxFrames` | `2` | Frames returned by one call (1 to 20): the pre-action reference and the settled end state. `computer_frames` is capped lower, at 16 |
| `maxAttachedImages` | `2` | Frames attached as images (0 to 19); further frames are still saved to disk and their paths printed |
| `changeThreshold` | `0.003` | Signature movement that counts as a change |
| `settleMs` | `700` | Extra capture after the action completes |
| `settleRunFrames` | `2` | Consecutive unchanged tail frame pairs required before the envelope calls the window settled |
| `maxWindowMs` | `15000` | Ceiling on one capture window (200 to 120000); also sizes the tool timeout |
| `maxWaitSeconds` | `10` | Longest passive watch |
| `maxTypeChars` | `2000` | Longest string computer_type accepts (up to 20000) |
| `maxScrollClicks` | `10` | Largest wheel gesture, in notches |
| `maxDragSteps` | `120` | Largest drag step count |
| `maxZoom` | `8` | Largest integer zoom (1 to 16) |
| `maxZoomedPixels` | `16000000` | Pixel ceiling for one zoomed capture, checked before any allocation |
| `frameMaxEdge` | `1024` | Longest edge of a captured frame |
| `frameQuality` | `75` | JPEG quality, 1 to 100, for the **in-process fallback** capture only; recorded frames are encoded by ffmpeg under `recorderQuality` |
| `ffmpegPath` | `ffmpeg` | Executable that records the screen |
| `tempRoot` | `` | Directory for the staged helper, recorder ring, screenshots, and markers; empty means a directory under the system temp directory. A drive root and an extended-length path are refused when the plugin activates, since with either one the recorder cannot be kept and every call would fall back to the in-process capture |
| `recorderQuality` | `5` | ffmpeg `-q:v` for recorded frames, 1 to 31; lower is better quality and larger files |
| `recorderBufferMs` | `4000` | Recorded video a call can reach back through for its own first frame |
| `recorderPrimeMs` | `400` | Recorder lead time before input is injected |
| `recorderIdleStopMs` | `30000` | Grace period before an idle recorder is stopped |
| `imageMode` | `auto` | `auto` attaches frames when the route accepts images and the attachment service is mounted; `text` never attaches. The route's own capability is still resolved, so the envelope can say whether `read_image` would work for a frame already on disk |
| `captureTimeoutMs` | `20000` | Timeout budget for a capture or probe call |
| `actionTimeoutSlackMs` | `10000` | Added to maxWindowMs for an action tool timeout |
| `compactionCleanupEnabled` | `false` | Delete this conversation's images once a compaction has summarised them. **Off by default**: the cleanup is implemented and tested, but eight adversarial reviews each fou

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness Web UI plugin: browser-style tabs for open Sessions - switch, close, reorder by drag, and tear a tab off into a separate window.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-tabs

Browser-style tabs for the Sessions a DeepSeek Harness window has open — switch, close, reorder by
drag, and tear a tab off into a window of its own, as a
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) client plugin.

Every Session the window has touched becomes a tab in a strip above the whole app. Click a tab to
switch to it, close it with `×` / middle click / the context menu, drag it left or right to reorder,
or drag it out of the strip to hand it to a new window. Closing a tab never deletes a Session —
exactly like closing a browser tab never deletes a page.

Nothing upstream is patched. The plugin registers into the official slot, locale and Session faces of
the web client, so it survives DSH upgrades and uninstalls by removing one row.

## What you get

- **Tabs for open Sessions** — one tab per Session this window shows, in the order you left them in.
- **Switch** — click a tab. If a global panel is open, the click returns to the conversation first.
- **Close** — `×` on the tab, the middle mouse button, or the context menu (`Close tab`, `Close other
  tabs`, `Close all tabs`). The Session itself stays in the sidebar and reopens with one click.
- **Reorder** — drag a tab left or right; the neighbours part as you go and the new order is written
  to this window's tab list.
- **Tear off into its own window** — drag a tab out of the strip and release: a hint appears under
  the cursor while the pointer is outside, and the Session opens in a new window. The context menu's
  `Open in a new window` does the same without dragging.
- **Restore** — the tab list of a window survives a page reload. A Session deleted in the sidebar
  loses its tab, and tab lists belonging to windows that are gone are dropped after 14 days instead
  of piling up in storage.
- **State dots** — a pulsing dot means that Session is working; a green one means it finished and has
  not been opened since.
- **Wheel scrolling** — the wheel over the strip scrolls it sideways when the tabs overflow.
- **Keyboard** — `Enter` / `Space` on a tab opens it, `Delete` / `Backspace` closes it; the strip is
  a `tablist` and the tabs are `tab`s.
- **New Session square** — the `+` at the left of the strip starts a Session through the client's own
  navigation service, so the reuse-or-create policy stays where it belongs.
- **Caption-row mode** — when the shell hands the page the window's title bar, the strip moves into
  the caption row itself and sits flush with the top of the window: the native Windows buttons stay
  native (Snap Layouts keep working) and their colours follow the live theme. Without that handover
  the strip is an ordinary band inside the page.
- **A strip that does not get in the way** — it starts to the right of the app's own leading
  controls and of the native window menu, and it is transparent to clicks except on its own controls,
  so the sidebar-collapse button underneath still works.

## Install

The package declares `dsh.client` (browser half) and `dsh.bundle.patch` (loader row), so it installs
like any other DSH plugin:

```sh
# from a checkout, or from a published copy
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <checkout>
# after that, reload the page once (a NEW row is picked up when the page's module table is built)
```

Manual mounting into a profile, which is what this repository was developed against:

```powershell
# 1. live link so edits are picked up by client HMR without reinstalling
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\<profile>\node_modules\dsh-session-tabs" `
         -Target (Resolve-Path .).Path

# 2. dependency of the profile:  $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/package.json
#    "dsh-session-tabs": "file:<path to this checkout>"

# 3. loader row:  $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml
#    - insert:
#        - id: session-tabs
#          name: dsh-session-tabs
```

The row belongs in the profile's patch layer rather than in `dsh.profile.bundles`, because the patch
layer reloads live: an edit to `lib/client.js` is picked up by client HMR without a restart, and a
page reload picks up everything else. A patch file must not be empty — use `[]` to disable the layer.

Rollback = drop the insert row, then reload the page; the dependency and the junction can stay, since
without the row the package is simply not mounted.

## How it works

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: an empty `apply()`, there only so the loader can mount the package and the client-modules scanner can find the `dsh.client` declaration |
| `lib/client.js` | The whole feature: the strip, the per-window tab store, the gestures, the caption-row handling, the tear-off hand-off |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The loader row a bundle install applies |

Five decisions worth keeping when editing:

1. **The strip is one entry in the shell's `shell.overlay` seat.** That seat is a click-through
   absolute layer above every column, so the strip can sit above the whole app. The frame itself is
   shifted down by the strip's height through a CSS rule keyed on the `data-dsh-session-tabs`
   attribute and the `--dsh-session-tabs-h` variable this plugin sets — the strip then occupies
   exactly the reserved band, drag handles included.
2. **Session identity and selection come from the official client services**: the Session
   Controller's list snapshot plus the workspace navigation service, which owns the current Session
   (`selection`, `openSession`, `startSession`, `clearMain`). A tab is just a Session id this window
   keeps around.
3. **Which tabs a window has is per-window state**: `sessionStorage` holds the window's own id (and a
   flag for a window born by tearing a tab off) and `localStorage` holds the tab list filed behind
   that id, under `dsh.session-tabs.v1:<window>`. That is what lets several windows show different
   Sessions at once and lets each of them restore its own tabs after a reload. A window handed a
   Session over `?dshTab=` always mints a fresh identity, because Chromium clones `sessionStorage`
   into script-opened windows and inheriting the source window's list would duplicate every tab.
4. **Tearing a tab off asks the shell for a real window.** The desktop shell exposes the preload verb
   `window.dshShell.openSessionWindow({ href, x, y, width, height })`, which the plugin calls with
   the drop point; anywhere else it falls back to `window.open` with a popup geometry. Either way the
   new window is handed the Session as `?dshTab=<sessionId>` on this page's own address, reads it on
   boot through the official `openSession`, and strips the parameter with `history.replaceState` — so
   the mechanism does not depend on who created the window. The launch token is not forwarded; the
   signed cookie is enough.
5. **The caption row is shared with chrome the page cannot see.** The window draws its own controls
   and its native menu bar in that band, and a translucent title bar lets the menu show through. The
   app's own controls are measured at runtime and the menu is reserved for; the strip then starts
   after both. The strip itself is `pointer-events: none` (its own controls opt back in) — otherwise
   it swallowed the click on the sidebar-collapse button, which then looked broken — and the free
   space after the tabs is a separate sibling drag region, because the strip must stay `no-drag` for
   tab dragging and wheel scrolling to work.

## Verify it yourself

```sh
# 1. syntax
node --check index.js && node --check lib/client.js

# 2. headless logic (93 checks): registration, the per-window store, restore, switching,
#    closing, middle click, reorder, tear-off into a new window, a refused shell,
#    the ?dshTab hand-off, housekeeping, the new-session square, and the caption-row geometry
node tools/smoke.mjs

# 3. a running GUI is serving THIS revision (needs a live host and its launcher log)
node tools/verify-live.mjs

# 4. the pre-publish gate: no personal data anywhere, no forbidden APIs in the payload
node tools/audit-public.mjs
```

`tools/smoke.mjs` runs the browser half against a mock React (hooks with persistent cells), a mock
DOM (elements, rects, `ref`, attribute queri

plugins.description: Local knowledge-graph memory tools for DeepSeek Harness
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tool-memory

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

Local knowledge-graph memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) as a Cordis plugin. The agent can store entities, observations, and relations in a file-backed graph, search them, and manage them across sessions — no external service and no credentials required.

## Install

```sh
npm install @libai168/dsh-tool-memory
```

Requires `@deepseek-ai/cordis` (^4.0.1) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (^0.1.0-rc.6) as peer dependencies.

## Configuration

```yaml
- name: 'github:LJH-snow/dsh-tool-memory'
  config:
    # storagePath: '~/.dsh/memory.jsonl'
```

The graph is stored as JSONL at `storagePath` (default: `~/.dsh/memory.jsonl`). The file format matches the official MCP memory server shape: entity lines carry `name`/`entityType`/`observations`, relation lines carry `from`/`to`/`relationType`, so an existing memory file can be reused as-is.

## Tools

| Tool | Description | Write |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_stats` | Report entity, relation, and observation counts plus storage path | No |
| `memory_read_graph` | Read the graph (entities, observations, relations) | No |
| `memory_search` | Search entities by keyword with related relations | No |
| `memory_create_entities` | Create entities from a JSON array | Yes |
| `memory_add_observations` | Append observations to one entity | Yes |
| `memory_create_relations` | Create relations between existing entities | Yes |
| `memory_delete_entities` | Delete entities and cascade their relations | Yes |
| `memory_delete_observations` | Delete specific observations | Yes |
| `memory_delete_relations` | Delete specific relations | Yes |

## Security contract

- Everything is local: the store reads and writes one JSONL file; there is no network access and no credential handling.
- Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and corrupt lines in an existing file are skipped on load instead of failing the plugin.
- Relations are only created between entities that already exist, preventing dangling references.
- Output is capped: reads return at most 200 entities and 500 relations, search returns at most 50 entities (default 20), names are capped at 200 characters and observations at 2,000 characters, and each mutating call accepts at most 100 input items.
- All mutating tools are marked `kind: 'edit'`; array parameters are passed as JSON strings and validated before any write.

## API scope

This version covers the full entity/relation/observation lifecycle with file storage. Timestamps, embeddings-based semantic search, and multi-store isolation are future work.

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm pack --dry-run
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: dsh插件，用于直接对客户端内或网页内的文字划线翻译
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-selection-translate · DSH 划词翻译

在 DSH 客户端里**选中任意文字**，旁边就会浮出一个「**译**」按钮；点一下，模型就地翻译并在选区旁弹出结果，可一键复制。

默认直接复用**当前会话正在使用的模型**（走 Host 端 `llm` 服务），因此**不需要另外配置 API Key**；也支持切到任意 **OpenAI 兼容端点**。

---

## 功能

| 能力 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 划词触发 | 鼠标选中文字（输入框、文本域、聊天记录、工具输出）后，选区旁浮出「译」按钮 |
| 一键翻译 | 点击后调用模型，结果在选区旁的浮层内展示 |
| 就近弹出 | 浮层自动避开屏幕边缘，超出视口时自动上翻 / 收进可视区 |
| 指定语言 | 浮层底部一排语言胶囊可即时切换目标语言并重译 |
| 智能中英互译 | 默认「智能」模式：中文→英文，其他语言→简体中文 |
| 复制译文 | 一键复制，兼容非安全上下文（回退 `execCommand`） |
| 双模型来源 | ① 当前会话模型（默认，零配置）② 自定义 OpenAI 兼容端点 |
| 设置界面 | 「设置 → 通用」新增一行：**开关 + 默认目标语言 + 「模型与端点设置」展开区**（提供商切换 / Base URL / 模型 / API Key / 测试翻译）。若该 profile 声明了 `settings.plugin.item`，插件页还会额外出现一张同样的卡片 |
| 隐私 | API Key 只存在 Host 端，**永不下发到浏览器**；浏览器只发 `{text, targetLang, sessionId}` |

## 交互

1. 用鼠标选中一段文字 → 选区右上角出现「**译**」按钮。
2. 点「**译**」→ 浮层出现，显示原文并开始翻译。
3. 需要换语言 → 点浮层底部的语言胶囊（`智能 / 简中 / 繁中 / EN / 日 / 韩 …`）。
4. 「**复制译文**」复制结果，「**重译**」重新请求，`Esc` 或点击空白处关闭。

> 键盘选择文字（`Shift + 方向键`）同样会触发按钮。

## 安装

本插件是一个标准的 DSH bundle 包，把整个目录作为一个本地包安装进 profile 即可：

```bash
# 在 DSH 检出目录下，使用桌面 profile
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<本目录绝对路径>/dsh-selection-translate
```

或者在该 profile 的 `package.json` 中把本包加进 `dependencies` 与 `dsh.profile.bundles`，然后重新加载 profile。

`cordis.patch.yml` 会把插件行插入 profile 的加载树：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-selection-translate
      name: dsh-selection-translate
```

装好后重启 DSH（或让 profile 热加载），选任意文字即可看到「译」按钮。

## 配置

配置文件落在 `~/.dsh/selection-translate.json`（`0600` 权限）：

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "targetLang": "auto",
  "maxChars": 6000,
  "temperature": 0.1,
  "timeoutMs": 60000,
  "provider": "current",
  "endpoint": "",
  "model": "",
  "apiKey": ""
}
```

| 字段 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | 划词翻译总开关 |
| `targetLang` | 默认目标语言，`auto` 为智能中英互译 |
| `maxChars` | 单次可翻译的最大字符数（超出会报错提示，避免误选超长内容） |
| `temperature` | 采样温度，翻译建议保持低值 |
| `timeoutMs` | 单次翻译超时（默认 60s） |
| `provider` | `current` 用当前会话模型；`external` 用下面的自定义端点 |
| `endpoint` / `model` / `apiKey` | `provider: "external"` 时使用，`endpoint` 需是 `/chat/completions` 完整地址 |

### 模型来源如何解析（`provider: "current"`）

Host 端按以下顺序取模型，取到即用：

1. 请求里带的 `sessionId` 对应会话的 `requestContext()/requestHeader()`；
2. `agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()`（即"默认模型"设置）；
3. 所有活动会话中最近一个可解析出模型的会话。

若都取不到，会提示你去输入框下方选择模型，或改用自定义端点。

## 内部接口（Host 端 HTTP 路由）

前缀 `/api/dsh-selection-translate`：

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/ping` | 健康检查 |
| `GET` | `/config` | 读取配置（**不含** `apiKey`，只回 `hasApiKey`） |
| `POST` | `/config` | 局部更新配置，返回脱敏后的完整配置 |
| `POST` | `/translate` | `{ text, targetLang?, sessionId? }` → `{ ok, text, provider, model, targetLang, ms }` |

翻译错误以 `{ ok: false, error }` 返回（HTTP 200），便于前端就地展示失败原因。

## 结构

```
dsh-selection-translate/
├── package.json          # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client 声明
├── cordis.patch.yml      # 把插件行插入 profile
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js          # Host：配置持久化、模型调用、HTTP 路由
│   └── client.js         # 浏览器：选区监听、浮层、设置界面
├── test/
│   ├── host.test.mjs     # Host 端 32 项：配置、prompt、路由解析、模型流、HTTP 面
│   └── client.test.mjs   # 浏览器端 14 项：选区→按钮→浮层→翻译→复制→设置
└── README.md
```

### 挂载的 Slot

| Slot | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `shell.overlay` | 全框浮动层：选区旁的「译」按钮 + 结果浮层（`replaceRisk: none`，纯追加） |
| `settings.general.item` | 通用设置里的偏好行；**完整配置都在这里**，因此必然可见 |
| `settings.plugin.item` | 可选的插件页卡片；某些组合（如本机 desktop profile）未声明该 seat，注册失败只告警、不影响其余功能 |

## 测试

两个自包含的校验脚本，不需要安装任何依赖（React 未落盘，脚本自带一个最小 React Hook 运行时 + DOM 桩）：

```bash
node test/host.test.mjs     # 32 checks
node test/client.test.mjs   # 14 checks
```

Host 端覆盖：配置读写与钳位、密钥不下发、损坏配置降级、prompt 组装、译文清洗、四级模型解析回退、流式分片收集、finish 错误/超时/空输出、外部端点请求体与错误透传、路由注册与释放、HTTP ping/config/translate。
浏览器端覆盖：三处 slot 注册、样式注入、无 slot 时不崩、**选区→按钮出现→点击→加载态→译文**、错误态、语言胶囊重译、复制、Esc 关闭、通用设置与插件卡片的读写、关闭时不渲染、选插件自身 UI 不自我触发。

## 已知边界

- **不覆盖 iframe 内的文字。** 文档预览里的 HTML 页（`iframe[data-html-preview]`）、侧栏浏览器页等位于独立文档，父页面的 `getSelection()` 取不到其中的选区，因此这些区域划词不会弹出按钮。本插件的选区监听只挂在主文档上。
- 选区监听基于 `selectionchange` + `mouseup`/`keyup`；`contenteditable`（如 Composer 输入框）走标准 `window.getSelection()` 路径，原生 `INPUT`/`TEXTAREA` 走 `selectionStart/End` 路径。
- `provider: "current"` 依赖 Host 端 `llm` 与 `sessions` 服务在场；缺失时会给出明确报错而不是静默失败。
- 自定义端点必须是 OpenAI 兼容的 `chat/completions` 协议。

## License

MIT

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-LGPL--3.0-blue)](LICENSE)
![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-8.0%2B-brightgreen)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/guzhou079-arch/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen?style=flat&label=stars)](https://github.com/guzhou079-arch/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen/stargazers)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin.
Tested with DSH on Android; the `adb` transport also works with DSH on a computer.

Looking for the whole thing ready to install on a phone (no PC, no Termux)? That is the
[Android port](https://github.com/guzhou079-arch/deepseek-harness-android) — same author, APK + in-app installer.

---

## Why

Most "agent drives my phone" plugins tap the **main screen**: your phone is hijacked while the agent
works — you can't use it, and it can't be used quietly in the background.

Android can create a **virtual display**: a second, invisible screen. The agent launches an app onto
that display, looks at it and taps it there, while the physical screen keeps doing whatever you were
doing. Every action reports a "main-screen proof" (`mainBefore` → `mainAfter`) so you can see the
physical screen was not touched.

## ⚠️ A virtual display isolates the **picture**, not the **effects** / 只隔离画面，不隔离副作用

An app running on a virtual display still acts on the **whole device**. Tap *Airplane mode*, *Wi-Fi*
or *Do not disturb* inside a virtual display and that switch really flips — it is the same system
setting. Installing, sending messages, changing settings: all real.

So *"your screen stays untouched"* is **not** the same as *"your device stays untouched"*.

**Rule for agents using this plugin:** take a frame with `android_vscreen_see` first, and derive tap
coordinates from what you actually see. Never tap a guessed fraction of the screen.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `android_vscreen_doctor` | Can I drive this device, and over which transport. Run it first. |
| `android_vscreen_status` | Is a virtual display running, and how big is it. |
| `android_vscreen_start` | Create the virtual display and optionally launch an app onto it. |
| `android_vscreen_see` | Grab a frame of the *virtual* display as a PNG. |
| `android_vscreen_tap` | Tap on the virtual display. |
| `android_vscreen_swipe` | Swipe on the virtual display. |
| `android_vscreen_close` | Destroy the virtual display. |

## How it reaches the phone

Two transports, picked automatically:

| Transport | When it's used |
|---|---|
| `adb` | DSH runs on your computer (USB or wireless debugging) |
| local bridge (`127.0.0.1:3081`) | DSH runs **on the phone itself** (e.g. the Android build) |

Both end up as a shell on the device — the same privilege level `adb shell` has. That privilege is
required: an app cannot put *another* app onto a virtual display with its own identity, so the
bundled core runs as `shell` via `app_process`. It uses only public Android APIs
(`DisplayManager.createVirtualDisplay`, `ImageReader`) plus documented reflection constants — **no
MediaProjection**, no screen-capture permission dialog.

## Install

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm, so several specs work. The release tarball needs neither git nor a clone:

```sh
# 1. release tarball (28 kB, no git involved)
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/guzhou079-arch/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen-0.1.0.tgz

# 2. straight from the repository
dsh plugin --profile web add github:guzhou079-arch/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen

# 3. from a clone you already have
git clone https://github.com/guzhou079-arch/dsh-plugin-android-vscreen
dsh plugin --profile web add link:./dsh-plugin-android-vscreen
```

The tarball is `dsh-plugin-android-vscreen-0.1.0.tgz`, 28227 bytes, SHA-256
`915369c3b42a3834636ee22e1dd0e8858fff48358c28ccb0590f9371988953f4`.

Where `github.com` will not open (mainland China), prefix the URL with a mirror — `https://ghproxy.net/`,
`https://ghfast.top/`, `https://gh-proxy.com/` — or use spec 3 against a clone fetched through one.

Then ask the agent to run `android_vscreen_doctor`: it reports which transport is available and
probes the device.

## Requirements

- An Android device reachable by `adb` (USB or `adb connect`), **or** DSH running on the phone with
  its privileged shell bridge available.
- Node.js 20+ (whatever your DSH runs on).

## Development

The device side is a small Java program in `assets/vscreen-core.jar`. To rebuild it from source, see
the Android port repository (`android-app/src/com/deepseek/harness/vscreen/`). Two smoke tests run
the whole chain without going through a model:

```sh
node test-m1.mjs            # create → launch → see → tap → see → main-screen proof → close
node vs-safe.mjs start      # same thing, but aimed at a harmless target
```

## License

**LGPL-3.0-only** — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) and [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
The bundled `assets/vscreen-core.jar` descends from [Operit](https://github.com/AAswordman/Operit)
(LGPL-3.0), which is why this plugin is LGPL rather than MIT.

plugins.description: 思考锚点：从模型上一段思考中提取已确立结论，在工具结果后注入，减少重复推导；并可识别打转与伪工具调用
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-cot-anchor

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件：治一类特定的模型毛病——**思考着思考，但没在推进**。表现为反复重新推导已经得出的结论、把工具调用写成纯文本、原地重复同一段话、输出无意义的递增数字流。

插件做两件事：

1. **结论回流**：每次工具结果返回后，从最新思考中摘出已成立的结论（最多 3 条、每条 ≤ 220 字）插回上下文，下一步起手就能看到，不必重推一遍。**装上默认生效。**
2. **生成中途打断（软切）**：生成过程中每 32 个字符检查一次，发现打转 / 原地重复 / 伪工具调用 / 数字流就立即切断本次请求，把已生成部分作为正常消息落盘、排好结论锚点，让回合从断点续跑——不会因为一次误判丢掉整轮工作。

它不解决一切长任务问题，只解决「单流内思考链极度冗余、结论反复重新发现」。跨步骤的折返跑（同一结论在十几步里重推）不在能力范围内，那是姊妹插件 [dsh-step-governor](https://github.com/JiewiW/dsh-step-governor) 的职责。

## 快速开始

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add github:JiewiW/dsh-cot-anchor#v0.3.0
```

重启实例后设置页出现「COT 锚点」标签即生效。结论注入无需任何配置；软切需要内核支持（见[兼容性](#兼容性与软切内核)）。

## 工作方式

```
模型思考 → 工具执行 → [插件] 摘出已成立的结论插回上下文 → 下一步思考
                                  ↑
                            只在工具边界注入
```

注入消息以 `user` 角色追加在工具结果之后、下一次请求之前，尾部追加写入会话日志，不改写已有内容，因此不会打穿前缀缓存。

## 成本

| 场景 | 额外成本 |
| --- | --- |
| 默认（结论注入开启，其余关闭） | 每个工具结果后一条短消息，上界 660 字符（3 条 × 220 字）；无额外模型调用 |
| 命令执行纪律提醒 | 每轮一次、随运行时上下文快照（"Current runtime context…"）注入，位于记忆规则之后；单条全文固定约 380 token（字符估算），作为稳定前缀段参与上下文，不再随工具调用堆叠 |
| 开启 LLM 提炼结论（默认关） | 每个助手回合**多一次**小模型调用 |
| 开启打转 / 重复等判定 | 纯本地字符串计算，零 token 成本；可能增加少量回合数 |
| 开启 CoT 静默采集 | 每个助手回合留一条本地样本；默认关闭 |

注入消息会随之后续请求的上下文一同发送，因此持续占用少量上下文窗口。按中英混排估算，660 字符约合 200–500 token 量级——相对于一次工具往返的上下文可以忽略，但它在**每一步**都会累积。注入以尾部追加方式写入会话日志，不改写已有内容，因此不会打穿前缀缓存：除新追加的一块外，此前内容始终是稳定前缀。新追加块在其首次出现的那次请求上按未命中计费一次，此后转为缓存命中——这一点与文本是否固定无关。推理锚点每次不同，其排列顺序仅为内容组织上的一致性，不影响缓存行为（自 411cb74/v0.2.2 起命令执行纪律已改走运行时上下文快照的固定段，不再参与本次工具注入）。

在一个约 924 万 token 的真实长会话上实测：插件注入总量约占全会话 0.23%（每个注入块只在首现那一次请求按未命中计费，此后转为缓存命中）。具体分项口径见下文「实测成本占比」。

## 能力边界（请先读）

- 两类机制都是**单步边界内**的：软切只看当前一次生成流，进入下一步计数归零。治得了单流内退化，治不了跨步骤折返跑。
- 软切不减少回合步数。长任务账单的大头是「步数 × 每步膨胀的上下文重读」，步数治理请用 step-governor。
- 模型可能**知道自己在空转却停不下来**——实测出现过思考中自述「I'm burning turns, let me stop」之后继续生成下一条探索路线。注入的前提是模型会读且照做，自知不构成刹车。
- 软切每回合按判定类别分桶计预算 **6/20/3**（启发式判定 6 次、字节级确证重复 20 次、伪工具调用 3 次），总闸 **29**（6+20+3）。打满后启发式判定升级为终止本回合，高置信重复仍照常拦截；预算事件（`agent/soft-cut-suppressed` / `phase.abortTurn`）在会话日志可观测。这些常量由内核定义、不由插件持有。

> 以下统计数据自 **v0.2.1 之前的机制**采集：当时命令执行纪律是随每次工具执行后剥出的独立 `user` 消息（`source.summary = cot-anchor: exec-discipline`）与推理锚点同车注入。**自 v0.2.1 起（并入 411cb74 迁移后）**，纪律不再随工具注入，而是注册为运行时上下文快照的一个固定段（每轮出现一次、位于记忆规则之后、用户唠叨之前），不再按工具条数线性堆叠；下述注入量只是旧机制的上限参照。

在一个 95 次助手请求、累计约 924 万 token 的真实长会话上按消息级口径统计（字符→token 为启发式估算，非 tokenizer 实测；任何人可在自己的 DSH 会话日志上按同口径复算：逐条统计 `user/message` 中 `source.summary` 为 `cot-anchor: exec-discipline`（固定纪律）与其他 `cot-anchor:*`（动态锚点）的文本，并对照各次助手请求 `usage` 的 `inputTokens` / `cacheReadTokens`）：

> 结论：插件带来的新增输入在全会话 token 总量的 0.3% 以内。每个注入块在首现时按未命中计费一次，此后随上下文增长参与后续每一次请求。纪律块体积约占注入量五分之四，但"文本固定"不带来额外缓存收益——该占比只反映体积，不反映命中。（该占比为 v0.2.1 之前旧机制的历史数据；新版纪律块已移入运行时上下文快照固定段，不再按工具条数累计。）

## 兼容性与软切内核

| 能力 | 支持的 DSH 版本 |
| --- | --- |
| --- | --- |
| 结论注入、设置页 | 0.1.5 起全部版本 |
| 生成中途打断（软切） | 仅 0.1.5-rc.1 / rc.2 开箱可用 |

0.1.5-rc.3 起内核移除了软切所需的 `agent/soft-cut` 钩子，该能力会静默失效；插件在启动日志和设置页顶部明确提示当前内核是否支持——**以设置页显示为准**，不要凭开关是开的就认为在生效。

新版内核可用随包工具把软切机构移植回去（带版本与哈希自检，幂等、可回滚，不符自动还原）：

```sh
node node_modules/dsh-cot-anchor/tools/apply-softcut-port.mjs --check   # 查看状态
node node_modules/dsh-cot-anchor/tools/apply-softcut-port.mjs           # 应用
```

移植后重启实例。完整步骤与风险见 [docs/softcut-kernel-port.md](docs/softcut-kernel-port.md)。

## 设置

设置页「COT 锚点」共 61 项、分组展示，多数场景用默认值即可。下面只列常用项与容易误判的项；其余阈值在设置页内均有内联说明。

### 总开关

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enableToolInject` | 开 | 工具结果后注入结论锚点，本插件的主要价值，建议保持开启 |
| `enableSoftCut` | 开 | 允许生成中途打断；内核不支持时自动无效 |
| `enableExecDisciplineBlock` | 开 | 随锚点同车注入命令执行纪律提醒；与锚点注入共用去重节奏，关闭后锚点注入行为不变 |

### 五项软切判定

全部关闭时插件只做结论注入。

| 键 | 识别什么 | 注意 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enablePseudoTool` | 把工具调用写成普通文本（如 `<seed:tool_call>...`） | 只能识别已知文本形态 |
| `enableRepeat` | 逐字节相同的内容反复吐出 | 换措辞的重复抓不到 |
| `enableChurn` | 措辞不同但反复「重新分析」 | 启发式判定，遇到未闭合代码块自动让路 |
| `enableTransition` | 「接下来我要……」类转折句 | **最容易误判**：正常分阶段思考也有转折句；若频繁在正常思考中切断，先关它（v0.3.0 起已要求转折词后跟随执行动词、并剥离已注入锚点后再判定，误判面已显著收窄） |
| `enableNumberRunaway` | 无意义递增数字流 | 要求数字流足够长（≥ 500 字符跨度等阈值） |

打断太频繁时：先关 `enableTransition`，其次调高判定阈值（`churnMinHits` 默认 18 等）。

自 v0.2.4 起，转折句判定自带「结论-转折间距」守卫（`softCutGapThreshold`，默认 80）：当尾部扫描窗口内最后一个结论开启词（如「所以」）与最后一个转折宣告（如「接下来」）间距超过阈值时，判定为「子阶段小结论 + 后续分析 + 转折宣告」而非阶段边界，拒绝软切——避免「所以 X 是根因」这类中途小结论与后续转折词各自命中检测器、把一次正常分析拦腰切断。

自 v0.3.0 起，转折句判定叠加三层加固（详见[发行说明](RELEASE-NOTES.md)）：① 已注入锚点按会话去重，同内容不再重复注入，命中时记录去重事件而非切断；② 「结论-转折间距」守卫在结论开启词缺失时由放行改为拒绝（fail-closed）；③ 切句与转折识别改为引号感知——报告正文中引用的推理原文、正则文本不再被切成以「所以/现在」开头的伪句；同时转折宣告词后必须跟随执行动词（「现在写报告」命中、「Now I have the full chain.」这类状态陈述不命中），已注入锚点文本也先剥离再参与判定，阻断「锚点自我触发」的自反馈环。

### 锚点内容

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `minReasoningChars` | 250 | 思考短于此长度不提取结论 |
| `maxPoints` | 3 | 最多保留几条结论 |
| `maxPointChars` | 220 | 单条结论字数上限 |

结论由规则从思考文本中摘句得到，不理解句子的语义角色，因此入池前会剔除两类无命题内容：纯话语标记句（剥掉 Actually / wait / Hmm / 其实 / 等等 等标记后实词不足 6 字符，如「Actually, wait.」「其实，等等。」）与路线意图宣告句（「the decisive route: ask the user…」）。标记词**领起但带事实命题**的句子（「Wait, the kernel never marks in verbose mode.」）照常保留。

注意：Wait / Actually / Hmm 等转折词在推理链中承担结构控制作用，插件**不从模型输出里删除它们**，只阻止它们被当成结论回灌。

### LLM 提炼与 CoT 采集（默认全关）

- `enableLlmRefine`：用一次小模型调用把整段思考压成摘要式结论，通常比规则摘句更准；provider/model 留空则跟随当前会话。
- `enableHarvest` / `enableAutoAnalyze` / `enableLearnedPatterns`：静默采集思考样本、自动归纳检测器看不见的打转形态、把学习成果用于判定。开启会在本地留存思考文本，启用前请自行评估隐私；学习模式默认有 20 轮影子期（`learnedShadowRounds`）防止一次误学永久改变判定。

## 隐私

- 结论注入与全部软切判定都在本地完成，不向任何外部服务发送数据。
- LLM 提炼开启时，思考文本会发给你指定的 provider（留空则跟随当前会话）。
- CoT 采集开启时，思考文本与工具轨迹只留存本地。

## 常见问题

**设置页显示「当前内核没有掐断能力」**
内核不提供软切钩子，结论注入不受影响。需要软切可停留在 0.1.5-rc.1/rc.2，或按上文移植。

**模型好像没收到提醒**
确认 `enableToolInject` 已开、且思考长度超过 `minReasoningChars`——思考过短本来就不提取。

## 开发

仓库根目录所有 `test-*.mjs` 都是独立可执行脚本（无测试框架、无 `npm test`），逐个 `node test-*.mjs` 运行，退出码 0 即通过。

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: DSH 插件：在会话“…”菜单的“归档会话”下方新增红色“删除会话”行，二次确认后真正删除该会话的日志与工作区登记（不可逆；当次启动使用过的会话先停用再删，正在执行任务的会话再点一次停止任务并删除）。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-delete

[English](README_EN.md) | 中文

给 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）会话“…”菜单的**“归档会话”下方加一个红色的“删除会话”**——真正删除该会话的全部数据，而不是只把它归档。

> 标签 / Tags: `dsh-plugin` · `dsh` · `deepseek-harness`

## 它做了什么

DSH 官方只提供“归档”（Archive），归档后的会话仍然留在磁盘上、也能在归档区找回。本插件补上**真删除**：

1. **菜单行**：在侧栏每个会话行的“…”菜单里、官方“归档会话”下方新增一行红色“删除会话”，带垃圾桶图标与分隔线。
2. **二次确认**：第一次点击变为“再次点击确认删除”（6 秒无操作自动还原），第二次点击才真正执行——菜单保持打开并直接显示结果，避免误删。若会话正有任务在跑，行会变为“再次点击：停止任务并强行删除”，再点一次先停任务再删；其他失败（宿主不可达等）行内显示原因并保持红色，再点一次即可重试。
3. **删除内容**：
   - 删除该会话在 `sessions/<工作区>/<会话id>/` 下的全部日志数据（含 `session.v4.jsonl.zstd`）；
   - 通过工作区注册表的官方持久化写清理登记（`unpin` → `unarchive` → `detachSession`），因此 `workspace.json` 由 registry 自己写，内存与磁盘始终一致，之后归档其他会话也不会把已删的会话“复活”。

## 安全性设计

- **当次启动使用过的会话也能直接删**：删除前先把该会话从内存停用（`flush` 落盘 → detach 会话 → 注销 agent，顺序固定——先会话后 agent，否则 DSH 会把行重新公告回来），写句柄随之关闭，日志删除带文件锁重试（15×100ms）——因此不会“删了不生效”或“删了又复活”，也不用重启。
- **正在跑任务的会话：提醒一下，再点一次就强删**：确认点击后若宿主返回“正在执行任务”，行会变为“**再次点击：停止任务并强行删除**”（6 秒无操作自动还原）；再点一次先调用官方 `workspace/session-stop` 停止任务（最多等 4 秒，可用环境变量 `SESSION_DELETE_STOP_WAIT_MS` 调整），任务拒绝停止也照样删——这是强行删除的既定语义。
- **删除成功后列表立即移除该行，无需重启**：插件会广播官方的 `api-session/removed` 事件（`dsh-api-remotes` 转发到每个浏览器），这正是 DSH 自己删除行用的通道——没有它，冷会话的行会留在浏览器启动时的快照里，掉进"未分组"直到重启。幂等的重复点击也会再广播一次，用来清掉残留的旧行。
- **鉴权继承官方通道**：删除接口挂在 DSH 共享的 `/api` 连接通道上（`connection.registerFetchRoute`），因此 Host/Origin 校验与浏览器认证由官方 `admit()` 统一把关。
- **幂等**：重复点击或对已删除的会话再次操作不会报错，只提示已删除。
- **不可逆**：删除会同时移除日志文件与登记，仅剩共享的附件/投影缓存等孤儿数据（无会话关联键，无害）。

## 安装

### 方式一：插件市场（推荐）

在 DSH 的插件市场（dshmarket）里搜索安装；仓库已按社区约定打标 `dsh-plugin`。

### 方式二：手动安装（github 源）

编辑 profile 的 `package.json`（`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`）：

```jsonc
{
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        // ... 其他 bundle
        "dsh-session-delete"
      ]
    }
  },
  "dependencies": {
    // ... 其他依赖
    "dsh-session-delete": "github:EarthPretender/dsh-session-delete"
  }
}
```

然后在 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`，重启 DeepSeek Harness。

### 方式三：本地目录

```jsonc
"dsh-session-delete": "file:./dsh-session-delete"
```

把本仓库放到 profile 目录下，同样需要加入 `dsh.profile.bundles`。

## 使用

1. 重启 DeepSeek Harness（首次安装后）。
2. 侧栏任意会话行 → “…” → 最底部红色 **“删除会话”**。
3. 第一次点 → “再次点击确认删除”，再点一次执行；结果直接显示在行内，**该行立即从列表消失**。
4. 若该会话正有任务在跑，会看到“再次点击：停止任务并强行删除”——再点一次即停止任务并删除。

安装后在 **设置 → 插件** 里可以看到本插件卡片，并可随时开关。

## 卸载

1. 从 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 与 `dependencies` 中移除 `dsh-session-delete`；
2. `pnpm install`，重启应用。

## 兼容性

- DSH `0.2.0-rc` 系列（Web / Desktop profile）。
- 宿主端为 Node ≥ 22；客户端半使用 DSH 平台基线模块（React、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`）。

## 结构

| 路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | **Host 半**：在 `/api` 上注册 `POST /api/session-delete`，执行日志删除 + registry 登记清理 |
| `lib/client.js` | **Client 半**：在 `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` 槽注册“删除会话”行 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle 补丁：插入一个同时承载两半的 loader 条目 |
| `icon.svg` | 插件卡片图标 |
| `scripts/selftest.mjs` | 零依赖自检（`npm test`），不需要启动 DSH |

## 开发自检

```bash
npm test        # = node scripts/selftest.mjs
```

自检不启动 DSH，覆盖三块：

1. **身份一致性**：`package.json` 的 `name`、`lib/client.js` 里 `__ModuleLoader__.load({ id })` 的 id、`cordis.patch.yml` 插入行的 `name` 必须三者相同。不一致时 client-modules 会报 `loaded without registering "…" via __ModuleLoader__.load`，浏览器半永远不会上场——设置页显示“本页面的插件未能完成同步”。
2. **浏览器半**：二次确认两步、忙碌会话的强删警告行（第三次点击带 `force: true`）、成功/被拒/网络异常三种结果、失败后可重试，以及槽注册的 name/id/order/locale。
3. **宿主半**：路由契约（`POST /api/session-delete`、buffered body）、非法方法/非 JSON/路径穿越、活动会话 409（未 force）、force 停任务（stop → flush → dispose → 注销 agent 的固定顺序）、stop 不生效时的有界等待、live 会话停用后删除、store 无法 detach 时的拒绝回退、真实删除（日志目录 + `unpin`/`unarchive`/`detachSession` + header 索引重建）、`api-session/removed` 广播、幂等与存储不可读时的 500。

> 改包名时（例如从 `@local/dsh-session-delete` 改成 `dsh-session-delete`）上面三处必须一起改，然后**重启应用**：已启动的页面仍持有旧 id 的客户端模块行，热改文件不会把旧行换掉。

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: A DSH plugin that welcomes users back to today's active conversations after a configurable idle period.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-welcome-back

DeepSeek Harness 的“欢迎回归 + 今日工作集”插件。

它只在你主动打开一个 DSH 会话时处理该会话：

- 只保存该会话最后一次可见消息的简短快照和时间戳；
- 自动跳过 DSH 的“用量 / 已完成 / 用时 / 时间戳”等界面状态行，以及工具过程卡片；
- 不读取长期记忆、其他会话、外部文件、Git 或系统活动；
- 闲置超过用户设置的阈值后，重新回到此会话时显示回归卡；
- 用户可以点击或直接按 `A`、`B`、`C`、`D`。

## 今日工作集（0.2.0）

默认提醒范围为“仅今日活跃会话”：

- 只有今天出现过实质性消息的会话，才会在下次回到该会话且超过闲置阈值时提示；
- 单纯打开一个历史会话不会把它加入今日工作集，也不会弹出历史闲置提醒；
- 插件不会主动扫描侧栏、逐个弹出、或打扰其他会话；
- 可改为“所有已记录会话”，或改为“仅手动加入的会话”；
- 在设置面板中可把当前会话加入或移出手动工作集。

“今天创建”依赖宿主是否暴露创建时间；本插件不猜测该时间。当前可靠规则是“今天出现过实质消息”。

## 笔记本界面与安全恢复（0.2.2）

- `◷` 默认在左下角，可直接拖动到任意位置；
- 右键点击 `◷` 可打开菜单：打开详细设置、恢复左下角、隐藏悬浮按钮；
- 隐藏后可按 `Ctrl+Shift+Alt+W` 恢复 `◷`。这是独立于 DSH 内置设置页的恢复入口；
- 回归卡的上一条消息区域有高度上限并可单独滚动；
- 回归卡整体在较小屏幕上可滚动，A/B/C/D 操作区固定在卡片底部，避免被长文本挤出屏幕。

## 当前原型行为

| 选择 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| `A` | 向当前会话发送“仅依据上一条消息复述明确的任务、约束和期待结果”的请求 |
| `B` | 向当前会话发送“仅依据上一条消息做极简断点汇报”的请求 |
| `C` | 关闭本次回归卡并继续 |
| `D` | 在最短重复提醒间隔内不再提醒当前会话 |

设置通过右下角的 `◷` 按钮打开。可配置总开关、闲置阈值、重复提醒间隔、提醒范围、是否显示时长和欢迎语。

## 安装与兼容性

当前版本为 `0.4.0`。它的代码与 `0.2.2` 完全相同，只是重新编号：`v0.3.0` 标签打在更早的一次提交上，那次提交引入的 DSH 内置设置页已在后续提交里移除，因此用 `0.4.0` 让最新版本拿到最大的版本号。本机验证在 DSH 内核 `0.2.0-rc.2` 上完成；重新编号不改代码，也没有测试更高的内核。本版本不注册 DSH 内置设置页，也不新增 DSH client inject 依赖。声明的兼容范围为：

```text
>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.2.1
```

可通过 DSH 的插件管理界面或插件命令安装本仓库。也可以下载 GitHub Release 中的 `.tgz` 预构建安装包。

安装或升级前应：

1. 确认 DSH 当前内核落在上述兼容范围内；
2. 备份 desktop profile 的 `package.json` 和 lockfile；
3. 完全退出 DSH Desktop；
4. 通过 DSH 的插件管理通道安装，而不是直接复制文件到 profile；
5. 重启 DSH 后，用一个短闲置阈值测试回归卡和提醒范围。

## 隐私与数据边界

插件在浏览器本地存储中仅保留当前会话的简短断点快照、活动时间、提示关闭时间和工作集标记。它不读取长期记忆、其他会话、外部文件、Git、项目状态或系统活动，也不会改写 DSH 会话日志。

plugins.description: tts tool that turns text into an audio file through any OpenAI-compatible TTS backend.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tts

Text-to-speech plugin for dsh: one `tts` tool that turns text into an audio
file (wav / mp3 / flac / aac / opus / pcm) through any OpenAI-compatible TTS
backend, so agents can voice their output without per-backend glue. The same
tool lists voices and models, probes the routes, and calls the backend's dev
phonemize endpoint.

## Tool verbs

| verb        | network | what it does |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------ |
| `synth`     | yes     | Synthesizes the requested speech. The tool writes the audio file to disk and runs container checks on the returned bytes. |
| `voices`    | yes     | Lists the backend voices, optionally filtered. When the backend returns 404 to `GET {baseURL}/audio/voices`, the tool serves the static OpenAI table and marks `source: static`. |
| `providers` | no      | Lists the configured routes with their fields, the originating layer of each field, and the credential state. The verb reads the local configuration and makes no network request. |
| `models`    | maybe   | Reports the model list of each route. A route with declared models reports the declared list from the config layer, and a route without declared models reports the live `GET {baseURL}/models` probe. |
| `status`    | yes     | Probes each route: the `GET {baseURL}/models` listing plus the optional server-root `GET /health` liveness probe. |
| `phonemize` | yes     | Calls the backend's `POST /dev/phonemize` endpoint at the server root. A 404 or 405 response reports the endpoint as unsupported. |

Key `synth` behaviors:

- The `voice` argument is required, and there is no default: the voice set is
  provider-specific. The available ids are listed by the `voices` verb.
- When the call omits `model`, the tool uses the route's single declared
  model. When a route declares no models, the tool resolves the model by a
  live `/models` probe. When the declared or probed model list contains
  several models, the call fails and lists the candidates.
- The `response_format` argument defaults to `wav`, and the tool sends the
  value verbatim.
- The backend owns container correctness, and the tool validates the returned
  bytes: a RIFF walk for `wav`, and magic checks for the other formats
  (`pcm` carries no container check). When the payload is not the claimed
  container, the call fails and the tool keeps the file on disk. When the
  container carries a known defect, for example the placeholder RIFF chunk
  sizes (`0xFFFFFFFF` or `0x7FFFFFFF`) some backends emit, the successful
  document reports it in `warnings`.
- When the call sets `out`, the output path is that argument (a file path, or
  a directory marked by a trailing separator or by existing on disk). When the
  call omits `out`, the tool writes the file to
  `<process.cwd()>/tts/<unixts>_<voice>.<ext>`. The file extension comes from
  the `response_format` value.
- The `speed` and `language` arguments are sent verbatim, and only when the
  call sets them.
- The synth timeout is 180 s, and the probe and phonemize timeouts are 15 s
  and 30 s.

The plugin ships a `dsh-tts` skill. The skill is the full tool reference for
agent contexts: it carries the parameter table, the env contract, and the
error shapes.

## Installation

dsh-tts is an out-of-tree plugin for a dsh profile. Install it with the dsh
plugin command:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-tts
```

Configuration is layered: built-in defaults, the `TTS_*` env contract, a
cordis patch file, a `dsh-tts` settings section (see below); the plugin
creates no config or state files.

## Configuration

Providers are configured in any of four layers, lowest to highest priority;
the `providers` verb reports the originating layer of every field, so a
shadowed value is never silent:

1. the built-in default (`api: openai-compatible`),
2. the `TTS_*` env contract (static per process boot),
3. the cordis config layer (a patch entry with id `dsh-tts` and a `config`
   object, or profile-level patches),
4. the `dsh-tts:` section in the user settings document
   (`$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`), which the plugin re-reads on every call, so
   settings edits apply without a restart.

```yaml
dsh-tts:
  defaultProvider: local
  providers:
    local:
      baseURL: http://<host>:<port>/v1
    hosted:
      baseURL: https://api.example.com/v1
      apiKeyEnv: TTS_HOSTED_KEY
      models: [kokoro-v2]
      displayName: Hosted Speech
```

The env contract mirrors the config fields 1:1: `TTS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`,
and per route `<NAME>` the variables `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_BASEURL`,
`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_API`, `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_APIKEYENV`,
`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_HEADERS`, `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_MODELS`,
`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_DISPLAYNAME`. The `<NAME>` segment is the route name
uppercased with `-` written as `_`. The `headers` value is a JSON object
string, and the `models` value is a comma-separated list of model ids. The
`baseURL` value is the OpenAI-compatible base URL including the `/v1` prefix
(the same shape as an LLM provider base URL); the plugin appends
`/audio/speech`, `/audio/voices`, and `/models` to it verbatim, and it
addresses `/health` and `/dev/phonemize` at the server root, which it derives
by stripping a trailing `/v1` from the base URL. The `apiKeyEnv` value is a
reference to an environment variable name, never a secret in config; per
request the value resolves from the process environment, then from
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.

## Examples

```jsonc
// Synthesize with the default route and its single declared model.
{ "verb": "synth", "input": "hello world", "voice": "zf_xiaoxiao" }
// Pick a route, format, speed, and output location explicitly.
{ "verb": "synth", "provider": "hosted", "input": "the quick brown fox",
  "voice": "zf_xiaoxiao", "response_format": "mp3", "speed": 1.1, "out": "/tmp/hi.mp3" }
// Find the voices by an id prefix filter.
{ "verb": "voices", "filter": "zf_" }
// Or by a case-insensitive substring over the id and name.
{ "verb": "voices", "query": "zf" }
// List what is configured, and where each field comes from.
{ "verb": "providers" }
// Probe the backend health (the live /models probe).
{ "verb": "status" }
// Ask the backend dev phonemize endpoint (a 404/405 response reports it as unsupported).
{ "verb": "phonemize", "text": "hello world", "language": "zh" }
```

## Troubleshooting

A failing call returns a JSON document with an `error` message field, and the
message text identifies the failure.

- When the error message is "TTS_NOT_CONFIGURED", no route survived
  configuration. Check the base URLs; the tool reports each route that
  configuration drops as a warning in the log.
- When the error message carries the text "credential missing: environment
  variable "X" is not set", the credential reference does not resolve. Set
  `X` in the environment or add it to `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.
- When the error message carries the text "unknown provider "x"", the route
  name matches no configured route. Route names match case-insensitively and
  treat `_` and `-` as the same separator; the error lists the configured
  names.
- When the error message carries the text "multiple providers configured
  (...) and no default is set", pass the `provider` argument explicitly, or
  set `TTS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`, or set the settings `defaultProvider`.
- When `status` reports `reachable: false`, the `error` field carries the
  cause; the probe uses a 15 s budget against `GET {baseURL}/models`.
- When `voices` reports `source: static`, the backend answered 404 to
  `GET {baseURL}/audio/voices`, and the tool returned the static OpenAI
  table. The listed voice ids may not exist on that backend.
- When the synth document carries a container check error, the tool could not
  verify the returned bytes as the claimed container. Inspect the kept file
  at `out`; the backend may return an unsupported container for the requested
  `response_format`.

## Build

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build     # tsc -> lib/
pnpm run lint      # eslint src/ test/
pnpm run selftest  # in-process: HTTP stub + config matrix + container checks
```

plugins.description: Android device automation tools for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): read screen, tap, type, back, launch app, swipe over a local HTTP bridge
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-android-tools

![test](https://github.com/asdukw/dsh-plugin-android-tools/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)

[DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com/harness/) (`dsh`) plugin that turns a device UI
automation bridge into agent tools: read the screen, capture frames, tap nodes/targets,
long press, type text, press system keys, launch apps and swipe.

This plugin is a thin, platform-independent HTTP client: it registers the tools and
forwards each call to a **bridge host** that implements the contract below. Reading the
UI tree and injecting gestures stays in the host. A reference host runs on Android with
an `AccessibilityService`, but any system that speaks the contract works with the same
plugin.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

## Requirements

- `dsh` running with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` >= `0.1.0-rc.6` (peer dependency).
- **A bridge host**: this repository ships the client half only — no host is published
  here. Point the plugin at an existing host, or implement the small contract below
  (see [Writing a host](#writing-a-host)); a runnable mock host is included for
  testing. Without a host, tool calls fail with a clear error.

## Tools

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `read_ui_tree` | Dump the current screen's node tree as lines like `[12] TextView "Send" clickable @(900,2200)` |
| `tap_node(ref)` | Tap a node from the last `read_ui_tree` |
| `capture_screenshot()` | Capture a **frame**: the image plus its frame info (image/screen size, `screenshot_id`) |
| `tap_target(screenshot_id,x1,y1,x2,y2)` | Tap a target you saw in that frame — bbox in **image pixels**, the host converts |
| `long_press_target(screenshot_id,x1,y1,x2,y2,duration_ms?)` | Long-press a frame target (default 700 ms, 300-2000 ms) |
| `long_press(ref,duration_ms?)` | Long-press a node from the last `read_ui_tree` |
| `type_text(text)` | Write text into the focused input; does not send |
| `press(key)` | Press `back` / `home` / `recents` / `enter`; use `back` for Esc-like cancel/exit |
| `launch_app(query)` | Launch an app by fuzzy name or package name |
| `swipe(direction)` | Swipe about half a screen `up` / `down` / `left` / `right` |
| `run_command(cmd,timeout_ms?)` | Run a shell command inside the phone's Linux (Termux + proot Debian); returns stdout / stderr / exit code |

`run_command` is not like the others: those **operate the UI** (reversible, visible), this one changes the
**filesystem** (no undo, nothing on screen). It is a real shell — `git` / `python` / `apt` / `npm` all work —
but every command is its own session (`cd`, env vars and background processes do not persist) and there is no
`docker` / `systemd` / `iptables` (proot is not a real kernel).

**It is only registered when the host injects `TAPPET_TERMUX_URL` and `TAPPET_TERMUX_TOKEN`** — hosts without
that setup never see a tool that is guaranteed to fail.

A `capture_screenshot` image only reaches the model through the **attachment service**
(`ctx.attachments`): the tool persists the bytes and returns an image content block. Without a
mounted attachment service it degrades to text (the call still succeeds, the image does not reach
the model) instead of failing. A bridge host just returns
`{ mediaType, width, height, base64 }` as the action `payload`.

The tools are app-agnostic atomic actions; the model composes them into tasks.

## Install

```bash
# from git, pinned to a release tag:
dsh plugin add github:asdukw/dsh-plugin-android-tools#v0.3.0

# or from the tarball attached to any GitHub Release:
dsh plugin add ./dsh-plugin-android-tools-0.3.0.tgz

# once npm publishing is enabled:
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-android-tools
```

The package ships a `dsh.bundle` layer (`cordis.patch.yml`) that inserts the plugin row
on install. Restart `dsh` afterwards.

## Configure

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ANDROID_BRIDGE_URL` | Bridge base URL, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:37812` |
| `ANDROID_BRIDGE_TOKEN` | Shared token checked on every request, usually random per host start |
| `TAPPET_TERMUX_URL` | URL of the phone's Linux bridge, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8899` (optional; without it `run_command` is not registered) |
| `TAPPET_TERMUX_TOKEN` | Access token for that bridge (optional; required together with the previous one) |

The host app or launcher normally injects both variables; they can also be exported
manually in the environment that starts `dsh`. If either is missing, every tool call
fails with `ANDROID_BRIDGE_URL/ANDROID_BRIDGE_TOKEN not set`.

## Usage

The intended loop is **read first, act, read again to confirm**:

```text
User: open the clock app and set a 5 minute timer
Agent: launch_app("Clock") → read_ui_tree → tap_node(12) → type_text("5") → …
```

To try the plugin without a device, run the bundled mock host (canned screen, no
device needed):

```bash
node examples/mock-host.mjs   # mock host on http://127.0.0.1:37812 (token: dev-token)
export ANDROID_BRIDGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:37812
export ANDROID_BRIDGE_TOKEN=dev-token
```

The mock acknowledges every action and returns a canned `read_ui_tree`.

## Bridge contract

```
POST {ANDROID_BRIDGE_URL}/action
header: x-android-bridge-token: <ANDROID_BRIDGE_TOKEN>
body:   { "action": "read_ui_tree" | "tap_node" | "long_press"
                    | "capture_screenshot" | "tap_target" | "long_press_target"
                    | "type_text" | "press" | "launch_app" | "swipe",
          ...action args }
```

Success: `{ "ok": true, "payload": "…" }` — failure: `{ "ok": false, "summary": "…" }`.

| Action | Args | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `read_ui_tree` | – | node-tree text, one node per line (`[ref] ClassName "text" [flags] @(x,y)`) |
| `tap_node` | `ref` (integer) | result summary |
| `tap_target` | `screenshot_id`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2` (image pixels) | result summary; `changed` says whether the screen moved |
| `long_press_target` | same as `tap_target`, plus optional `duration_ms` | result summary; `changed` |
| `long_press` | `ref`, plus optional `duration_ms` | result summary |
| `type_text` | `text` (string) | result summary |
| `press` | `key` (`back` / `home` / `recents` / `enter`) | result summary |
| `launch_app` | `query` (string) | result summary |
| `swipe` | `direction` (`up` / `down` / `left` / `right`) | result summary |
| `capture_screenshot` | – | JSON string `{ "mediaType", "width", "height", "screenshotId", "screenWidth", "screenHeight", "offsetX", "offsetY", "base64" }` |

`press_back` remains an optional legacy bridge alias for `press(back)`, but it is not
registered as a model tool. Keep the bridge local (e.g. loopback) and token-checked:
screen content can be personal data, and the bridge can drive the device. Payloads are
only returned to the model; do not log them.

## Writing a host

A host is any process that can read the UI and inject input. The contract above is the
entire interface:

| Where the host runs | Typical building blocks |
|---|---|
| Android | `AccessibilityService` (`getRootInActiveWindow`, `dispatchGesture`, `ACTION_SET_TEXT`, …) |
| Windows | UI Automation |
| macOS | Accessibility API (`AXUIElement`) |
| iOS | WebDriverAgent / XCTest |
| Anything else | whatever can produce `read_ui_tree` text and accept taps |

Checklist:

- listen on loopback (or authenticate hard) and verify `x-android-bridge-token` on
  every request;
- map `action` + args to the platform primitives and return `{ok, payload}` or
  `{ok, summary}`;
- `read_ui_tree` must emit one line per interesting node in the documented format — the
  model relies on `[ref]` staying stable until the next read so `tap_node` works;
- keep ROM/OEM quirks inside the host so the tool surface never changes.

`examples/mock-host.mjs` is a ~60-line reference for the parsing/auth/reply shape.

## Platform notes

- The plugin contains no OS-specific code — it only speaks HTTP. Porting to another
  platform means writing a bridge host, not changing the plugin.
- ROM/OEM behaviour (accessibility permissions, gesture injection quirks, node-tree
  differences) belongs behind the bridge, so the tool surface stays stable.

## Generic boundary

This plugin intentionally exposes only app-agnostic primitives. Chat, shopping, settings
and other busines
